items.bio: Polyagentmorous ClawFather. Came back from retirement to mess with AI and help a lobster take over the world. @OpenClaw🦞 + @OpenAI
items.summary_en:
The biggest design mistake I made when we moved OC to sqlite: using sync db access. When it was just an agent that reports to you on Slack or iMessage this was fine; now that one agent might do 50 sessions in parallel and the whole team works on it, it is limiting.

I have a /goal with Astra that so far landed 575 PRs to move everything to to async workers. We ship these improvements as we make progress. Pretty insane how even huge refactors are no longer scary.
items.summary_zh:
把 OC 迁到 sqlite 时最大的坑，是用了同步数据库访问；单个 Slack/iMessage 汇报型 agent 还能扛，到了一个 agent 并行 50 个 session、全团队共用时就成了瓶颈。

他们用 Astra 的 `/goal` 已经落了 575 个 PR，把系统迁到 async workers；现在连这种巨型重构都不再吓人。

items.author: Aaron Levie
items.bio: ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
items.summary_en:
You can’t automate what you can’t measure. This means that evals are one of the gates to diffusion of AI in the enterprise. 

We can test our deterministic processes through software, but most enterprises have no useful way of understanding how their non-deterministic processes are working today. Specifically the work that agents are doing for them.

Evals are mission critical for enterprises adopting AI because you have no other way of knowing what’s working, what’s broken, what changed, what improved, what you can do more of, etc. if you don’t have a good sense of how agents work in your environment today. All changes, upgrades, and deployments are downstream from good evals.

Not only are we going to get vastly more domain specific evals over time for the labs and across the industry, but every enterprise will also need a clear sense of how agents are performing in their environment as well. Huge opportunity.
items.summary_zh: 企业 AI 推不动，很多时候不是模型不够强，而是压根没法衡量 agent 在真实业务里干得怎么样。Evals 会成为企业部署、升级和扩展 AI 的闸门：没有好评测，就不知道什么有效、什么坏了、什么变好了，更谈不上自动化。

items.author: Sam Altman
items.bio: The mission of OpenAI is to ensure that AGI benefits all of humanity
items.summary_en:
There is an extensive and ongoing review related to our agents’ use of internet access during training and evaluation. We’ve been publishing summaries at the link below and will continue to.

We have not been as fast as we would have liked but we are trying to balance our desire for transparency with gaining a clear understanding from petabytes of agent activity logs, and working with impacted organizations.

We are prioritizing as best as we can based on severity, and adding resources. Hugging Face is still the most severe event we’ve seen. We will be as transparent as we can be subject to things like vulnerabilities in other companies that our agents have found, which will be their call to disclose or not.
items.summary_zh: 他们正在复盘训练和评测中 agent 上网行为带来的问题，但进展不够快，因为要从海量日志里厘清事实、同时处理受影响机构。Hugging Face 仍是目前最严重事件；涉及其他公司漏洞的部分，不会由他们单方面公开。

items.author: Guillermo Rauch
items.bio: @vercel CEO
items.summary_en:
We're helping world-class organizations like @klaviyo build agentic deployment platforms.

① Connect every agent (claude, codex, cursor…)
② Configure SSO via their IDP (Okta, Entra)
③ Now everyone can cook, securely®

What happens to SaaS once every company sets this up? I get this question a lot 😁

First, the data must come from somewhere. These apps only work if they can be infused with business data.

This is why we see the big enterprise SaaS players suddenly prioritize shipping CLIs and MCPs. Or dust off APIs they were neglecting for years.

The new 'procurement bar' will be how ergonomic your product is for *agents*, rather than humans. How easily they can navigate your ontology and work with your data.

Once that's in place, there's a long tail of SaaS applications that I suspect will never be bought again. They'll be generated. They'll be more secure, more performant, more modern, and tailored to each company's and employee's needs.
items.summary_zh: 企业 SaaS 的新采购门槛会从“人好不好用”变成“Agent 好不好用”：CLI、MCP、API 和业务数据本体才是入口。等每家公司都有安全的 agentic 部署平台，一大批长尾 SaaS 不会再被购买，而是被按需生成。

items.author: Boris Cherny
items.bio: Claude Code @anthropicai
items.summary_en:
Tag writes >50% of my PRs every day. It also does ~100% of my data analysis, and fixes most of our product feedback + bugs.

It's not like a regular Slack bot. It is proactive, programmable, it has memory, it has access to your connectors. With Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1, it has strong judgement.

Example prompts I use:

- "@Claude react to threads in this channel with ✅ when resolved"
- "@Claude from now on, attempt to repro every bug in this channel end to end, running the full app. once you reproduce the bug, put up a pr to fix it and tag the right team for code review"
- "@Claude brainstorm ~100 hypotheses for what could explain this weird data, use a workflow to in/validate. spend 10m tokens or so digging very deep. draw a chart with the result."
- "@Claude make me an interactive game explaining how this part of the code works, then make a slide deck explaining it for others on the team"

https://t.co/gmsALM8Lvs
items.summary_zh:
Tag 已经不是 Slack 机器人，而是一个能写 PR、跑数据分析、复现并修 bug 的主动型工程同事；每天一半以上 PR、几乎全部数据分析和大量产品反馈处理都交给它。

关键差别在于它可编程、有记忆、接入各种工具，还能用强模型做判断：从自动标记已解决线程，到端到端复现 bug 提 PR，再到烧千万 token 深挖异常数据、做图、做游戏和幻灯片。

items.author: No Priors
items.title: Re-Founding Incumbents for the AI Era with Sequence Holdings Co-Founder and CEO Michael Lee
items.summary_en:
Speaker 1 | 00:00 - 00:25
Every company on the planet has a celebrated persona. In a world where you believe that alpha comes from engineering and AI, you need to create a culture whereby the celebrated persona is the engineer, and that's what's required. You think about your typical investment in a fund, and you're typically trying to figure out how do we start to package to sell this thing in three That is just a very different framing for how we think about technological transformation and what what are the investments you're willing to bring to bear here. What we do is scarce. We're trying to do one deal per year.

Speaker 1 | 00:25 - 00:26
That's it. Our job is to do one.

Speaker 2 | 00:33 - 00:58
Hi, listeners. Welcome back to No Priors. Today, I'm here with Michael Lee, cofounder and CEO of Sequence Holdings. They just announced the largest AI take private to date with the Dell family office of Baldwin for $7,700,000,000. We talk about this, the Sequence story, how AI transformation is actually going to permeate the economy and what transfers from public investing to private equity to operating.

Speaker 2 | 00:58 - 01:01
Welcome, Michael. Michael, thanks for doing this.

Speaker 1 | 01:01 - 01:02
Thanks for having me.

Speaker 2 | 01:02 - 01:18
So you started Sequence Holdings, which is a permanent holding company that works with management teams to buy and refound their businesses to be market leaders with AI. We should talk about that, and it's a very exciting model. But you also announced this big transaction in Baldwin. Tell us about it.

Speaker 1 | 01:18 - 01:53
Yeah. You know, we started the company twenty months ago really with an eye towards can we partner with world class businesses and management teams, working closely with our frontier engineering t
items.summary_zh: AI 时代重塑传统企业，核心不是包装三年后卖掉，而是把工程师变成公司最受尊崇的人，并用工程与 AI 重新定义文化和投入。Sequence 的打法极稀缺：一年只做一笔交易，把企业买下来后长期重建。
